turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): I am very sorry, doctor, for coming late. The auto was held up at the circle for almost twenty minutes, and my wife got quite worried.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please, that is quite all right. Do sit. Afternoon traffic does this to everyone.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you. She is waiting outside with the discharge file. I said I would speak with you myself.
[SEG0004] person_3 (NURSE): Sir, before we go on, your blood pressure just now is one thirty eight over eighty six, and the pulse is seventy two, regular.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. One thirty eight over eighty six. Steady enough. So, what is troubling you today?
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, the thing I came for is the weakness in my left hand. It is still there.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): After the stroke, I take it. How long ago was that?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Three months back. They told me it was a mild stroke. The left hand became weak that very day.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. And the speech, the walking, I want to separate what has come back and what has not.
[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm. The speech was slurred for about a week, then it cleared fully. Walking is all right if it is a short distance. Err, if I walk a long way, the left leg feels heavy.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any headache? Any fit, or a blackout?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): No, doctor. No headache, and no fits or blackouts.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Shortness of breath?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.

[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me check. Squeeze my fingers, both hands. The left grip is weaker than the right, no droop of the face. Speech is clear, and you walked in steadily with no drag of the foot.
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): It is only slight, doctor. I can hold a cup. Buttons are difficult, that is all.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am thinking it through. A new stroke would more often pull in the speech or the leg again. My impression is residual weakness from that mild stroke, not a fresh event.
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): I am relieved to hear that. I did fear it was starting once more.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tell me the tablets you actually take, with the dose if you have it.

[SEG0020] person_1 (PATIENT): Aspirin 75 milligrams every morning, atorvastin forty at night, and amlodipine, one tablet of five milligrams, in the morning, for the pressure. I stopped the clopidogrel after three weeks, as the hospital doctor advised. They spoke of warfarin, but I was never given that one.

[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Clopidogrel for a few weeks and then stop, that is correct, so it stays stopped. Continue the aspirin, the atorvastatin and the amlodipine just as you are taking them. Do not restart the clopidogrel.
[SEG0022] person_1 (PATIENT): I have been regular with them, doctor. The morning tablets I do not miss.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): The pressure itself, since when?
[SEG0024] person_1 (PATIENT): High blood pressure for about eight years. The stroke is the only other illness.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family, anyone with sugar, pressure, heart trouble, stroke?

[SEG0026] person_1 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, my mother did not have sugar, and my elder sister has pressure but no sugar. My younger brother had a heart attack at forty eight. Nobody else, doctor.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): And your work, the hours, food, exercise, alcohol?

[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): I am an accounts clerk in a textile firm, nine to six, six days a week, mostly sitting. Diet is simple vegetarian, rice, dal and vegetables, and I have reduced the salt. I walk in the colony for twenty minutes every evening. I do not take alcohol, and I have never smoked.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Good. Salt down and that walk can continue. For the hand, open and close the fist and pick up small things like buttons, ten minutes, twice a day.
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): Certainly, I will do that. My neighbour said I must have an MRI, so I thought I should ask you.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Neighbours mean well, but let me decide this one. We might do an MRI of the brain if the hand weakness does not settle. I am not booking it today.
[SEG0032] person_1 (PATIENT): I understand. Of. I will not chase the scan on my own.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come and see me in six weeks. If the weakness suddenly increases, or the speech goes slurred again, do not wait, come the same day.
[SEG0034] person_1 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. You have explained it clearly. I will come in six weeks, and I will take my wife and the file and go.

spec.situation: Patient three months after a mild stroke with a spouse; slight weakness in the left hand; takes aspirin, atorvastatin and an amlodipine tablet; blood pressure read aloud; walking and speech discussed.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

omissions.text: Patient said walking is all right for short distances.
Patient can hold a cup but buttons are difficult due to the hand weakness.
Clopidogrel was stopped after three weeks as advised by the hospital doctor.
Warfarin was discussed previously but the patient was never given it.
Doctor specifically advised that clopidogrel should remain stopped and not be restarted.
Stroke is the only other illness apart from hypertension.
Family history also included mother did not have diabetes and elder sister has hypertension but no diabetes.
Doctor advised to continue reduced salt intake ('salt down').
MRI of the brain was specifically not being booked today.
